sonnet.problem: The card says 'Daughter of Zion' is 'a name for Jerusalem (Micah 4:10)'. Micah 4:10 does not say outright that the two names mean the same place. The card also says Micah 'has been speaking to' the Daughter of Zion, which links the earlier verses together more than the cited text states.
sonnet.rule: He says two names mean the same person only when a verse says so outright, and he gives that verse.

sonnet.problem: The statement 'someone comes along to rescue the sheep' reads 'them' in 'with no one to rescue them' as the sheep. The text does not say whether 'them' means the sheep, the beasts or someone else. The card settles what the text leaves open.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: The card calls horses and chariots 'two things meant for battle'. Verse 10 does not say this, so the card adds a purpose the text doesn't give. The phrase also steers the baker toward 'chariots' on the next fill-in-the-blank card.
sonnet.rule: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.
